content.text:
# Recursion Explained for Beginners

Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it into smaller, similar sub-problems. Each time the function calls itself, it works on a simpler version of the original problem, getting closer to a basic case that can be solved directly without recursion. The most important part is the "base case"—a simple condition where the function stops calling itself and returns a direct answer, preventing infinite loops. Once the base case is reached, all the function calls stack up and return their results back through the chain, eventually giving you the final answer.
